name: Crying in Your Face
editorial_article: "Crying in Your Face" is a seminal electronic track by Richard D. James, operating under his AFX moniker, originally released as the opening cut of the fourth installment in his acclaimed *Analord* series in 2005. The track later saw wider distribution on the 2006 compilation album *Chosen Lords*. As part of the *Analord* project, which was notable for its dedication to analog synthesis and vintage Roland equipment, "Crying in Your Face" serves as a masterclass in textures and repetitive, hypnotic motifs. \n\nMusically, the track is defined by its stuttering, syncopated acid-techno pulse and a distinct vocal sample—"My boyfriend was crying in New York"—that repeats with a mechanical, obsessive quality. This repetition strips the vocal of its initial narrative weight, transforming it into just another rhythmic layer within the dense, hardware-driven arrangement. The production showcases James's signature ability to balance aggressive, squelching low-end frequencies with delicate, almost fragile melodic glimmers. Its inclusion in the *Analord* series solidified its place in the canon of 2000s IDM and acid-techno, representing a pivotal moment where analog hardware purism collided with avant-garde composition. The track remains a cult favorite for its technical precision and its eerie, lingering emotional resonance.
